readerQuestion: Will the IRS refund my unused adoption credit carryforward automatically?
demandSource: DataForSEO 2026-10-28 (us): 'adoption tax credit refund' 210/mo, 'adoption tax credit carryforward' 70/mo KD 19, 'form 8839' 880/mo KD 18; fresh-trend rule applied (IRS release Oct 16, 2026); SERP winnable, AI Overview cites irs.gov, natptax.com, turbotax, yahoo finance
decisionGap: Readers with a 2020-2024 carryforward cannot tell from the headline whether they must act, what the notice means, and what it does to their 2026 carryforward.
method: No test or model. Basis is reported IRS guidance read in full on 2026-10-28, plus synthesis into a who-must-act decision path.

provenance.scopeAndLimits: Page restates and organizes IRS statements. No refund amounts are computed because the IRS publishes no formula for how much of a carryforward becomes refundable.
provenance.publicMethod: Sources linked in-line and in the Sources list.
provenance.placement: Third-person attribution to the IRS beside each finding; Takeaway section names the IRS announcement and questions and answers as the basis.

findings.claim: 2020-2024 carryforwards can raise the 2025 refundable amount, up to $5,000 per eligible child
findings.label: reported

findings.claim: No amended return is needed; filers who filed before 2026-04-15 generally get it automatically
findings.label: reported

findings.claim: Where's My Refund will not show the adjustment
findings.label: reported

findings.claim: 2026 refundable cap is $5,120 per child; the 2025 treatment does not carry into 2026
findings.label: reported

findings.claim: Refund amount for any given family
findings.label: unknown

counterexample: Extension filers, accounts with identity theft indicators/freezes/dependency conflicts, filers who never claimed the credit, and filers whose refund is offset against other debts do not simply receive $5,000 per child automatically.
exclusions: No TESTED format: tax guidance is a financial/professional-service topic outside _experience.md section G; no executed tests exist.
unknowns: 2025 maximum credit and phaseout (not on the pages read)
whatWouldChangeTheRecommendation: A revised IRS announcement, a change to the $5,000 cap, or an IRS statement that extension filers must act.
selectedMedium: text with one small comparison table (2025 adjustment vs 2026 rule); no calculator because no published formula supports one
noteOnScoutDate: Scout email said IRS/Treasury clarified on Oct 28; IRS release IR-2026-123 is dated Oct 16, 2026. Page uses the IRS date.
